clue.text: Broadcast from engineer needing outside assistance

indicators.note: the engineer needs the word for assistance placed outside him, so it wraps round

parts.note: aid is help or assistance
RE is the Royal Engineers, the usual crossword engineer

explanation.surface: Something is transmitted by an engineer who has to call in outside help.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aired has been transmitted on radio or television, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Metal bench on terrace lacks dash

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a pew is a church bench

indicators.note: the word terrace goes without the letters of a word for dash, which are removed

parts.note: taken as written before the removal
a race is a dash, a sprint

explanation.surface: A metal bench out on a patio is missing some flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Pewter is a grey alloy of tin, an example of a metal.

clue.text: Radical porter's drink?

parts.note: radical comes from Latin radix, a root
porter is a dark beer; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: An extremist doorman's beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a doorman, but it is a dark British beer; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Root beer is a sweet fizzy soft drink flavoured with sassafras, a kind of beverage.

clue.text: Making one hard to listen to you within home circle

indicators.note: the sound of the word you is placed inside the words for home and circle

parts.note: in means at home
a ring is a circle

indicators.note: the word you is heard rather than written, giving its sounding letter

parts.note: the word said aloud, sounding like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone finds it hard to hear you inside the family circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Inuring is accustoming someone to hardship, toughening them, a gerund synonym.

clue.text: Worker's party depressed queen

indicators.note: in a down answer the queen is pushed down, below the party, so she comes after it

parts.note: Labour is a British political party
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: The workers' political party has left the monarch feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker's' is read as 'Worker is'; Labour is the UK's left-of-centre party.
explanation.definitionFit: A labourer does manual work, so is an example of a worker.

clue.text: Part of wheel that's been in rut, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of these words could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A bit of a wheel that has been stuck in a groove.
explanation.definitionFit: An inner tube is the inflatable ring inside a tyre, one component of a wheel.

clue.text: Conservative's obscure leap forward

parts.note: to obscure is to hide from view
a bound is a forward leap

explanation.surface: A Tory's mysterious jump ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative's' is read as 'Conservative is'; it is not the party here.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidebound means narrow-minded and resistant to change, a synonym of traditionalist.

clue.text: Pubs incorporate new buildings for storage

indicators.note: the pubs take a letter into their body, so it goes inside

parts.note: bars are pubs

explanation.surface: Pubs absorb newly built storehouses.
explanation.definitionFit: Barns are farm buildings used to store grain and hay.

clue.text: All that sort of music?

definitions.meaning: from the phrase 'and all that ...', meaning and so on, all that stuff
a style of music with improvisation and swing

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'and all that jazz' means everything of that kind, and the word also names a musical genre born in New Orleans.

clue.text: One willing to try new rota

parts.note: to test is to try

indicators.note: new says the letters of rota are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone keen to try out a new duty roster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ROTA to ATOR. 'One willing' is a pun: one who makes a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will, so the definition is a pun on willing.

clue.text: Bird books only cover eagles, tracing their origins

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible, a set of books

indicators.note: the origins of the four words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A bird book that covers only eagles, tracing where they come from.
explanation.walkthrough: AV, the Authorised (King James) Version of the Bible, stands for 'books'.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upturned bill.

clue.text: Elm road cut off at both ends

indicators.note: the word for road loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a street is a town road

explanation.surface: An elm-lined road is blocked at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An elm is a type of tree, so the definition is an example.

clue.text: Article backed unknown earthquake town

indicators.note: backed says the article is turned to face the other way

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y
read as earth quake: the letters of earth are shaken up, the second half of the word acting as the anagram signal

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece reported a town hit by an unknown earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: The town is not hit by a quake: the word splits in two, with its second half rearranging its first, and 'backed' turns the article round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nazareth is a town in Galilee, the hometown of Jesus.

clue.text: Middle-class brogue, so I become confused

indicators.note: the letters of these words are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone muddles a middle-class shoe, getting confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Bourgeois describes the comfortable property-owning social group, a synonym of conventional middle-class.

clue.text: Two presents in place? Not at all!

parts.note: now is present in time
here is present in place

explanation.surface: Asking if two gifts are where they should be, and being told no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presents' looks like gifts but means the present time and the present place.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in no location at all is to be absent from anywhere.

clue.text: Pressured environment that's very popular with theatre audience

parts.note: something hot is very popular, in demand
the house is a theatre's audience, as in a full house

explanation.surface: A tense setting that goes down well with playgoers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothouse is an intense setting that forces rapid development, a figurative greenhouse.

clue.text: An author's attribute

parts.note: a scribe is a writer; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A characteristic belonging to a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attribute' is the verb (to credit), not the noun its surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe is to credit something to a cause or person, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Stripper?

parts.note: suggests paint remover, but read as a woman who strips on stage in a revue

explanation.definitionFit: A dancer in a stage revue may perform a striptease, so the cryptic hint describes such a performer.

clue.text: Hybrid lemon developed outside Greece

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside the abbreviation for Greece
developed says the letters of lemon are worked into a new form

parts.note: GR is the international abbreviation for Greece

explanation.surface: A cross-bred lemon is grown beyond Greek borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges LEMON to MONEL, which goes 'outside' GR.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel is a dog of mixed breed, a crossbreed.

clue.text: Sort of music alternative put into speech, almost

indicators.note: the alternative is placed inside the shortened speech
almost says the word for speech loses its last letter

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A kind of music offered as an option within a near-complete address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the speech's final letter, and 'put into' places the option inside what is left, just before its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large choral work on a sacred theme, a musical genre.

clue.text: Told to lift beams

indicators.note: told says the word is spoken, so its sound is used

parts.note: the word said aloud: to raise is to lift

explanation.surface: Someone instructed to hoist the girders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beams' looks like timbers but means shafts of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are beams of light, a plural synonym.

clue.text: Some resistance to acting for the crown

definitions.meaning: a quantity of electrical resistance, measured in its units
initials for On Her Majesty's Service, printed on British official mail; to reads as a joining word

explanation.definitionFit: Units measuring electrical resistance, and the initials marking British official business done for the monarch.

clue.text: The threat of people getting a hole in one

parts.note: men are people
in golf a hole in one is called an ace

explanation.surface: The danger posed by golfers scoring an ace.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a danger or source of intimidation, a synonym of threat.

clue.text: Precious little joy getting into British island university

indicators.note: the shortened joy goes inside the British island university
little says the word joy is cut short, losing its tail

explanation.surface: Hardly any happiness at a British island college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious little' looks like one phrase, but 'little' cuts JOY to JO, which goes 'getting into' B I U.
explanation.definitionFit: Bijou describes something small and elegant, so dainty and treasured.

clue.text: Store — in a computer — lines following brief note

indicators.note: the lines come after the brief note

parts.note: a memo is a short note
RY is short for railway, railway lines

explanation.surface: Save a file on the computer, then write lines after a quick memo.
explanation.definitionFit: Memory is the part of a computer that stores data.

clue.text: Big caper on carriage

indicators.note: in an across answer, the caper placed on the carriage comes after it

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled horse carriage
an antic is a playful caper

explanation.surface: A huge prank played on a horse-drawn cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic means enormous, a stronger synonym of large.

clue.text: Happy end to case of scurvy

parts.note: a tip is an end

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cheerful finish to a bout of a sailor's disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy' here means merry from drink; 'case of' looks like an instance of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang happy can mean slightly drunk, the same as merry.

clue.text: One who maligns lower classes rural transport

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at working people's farm vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research grades society from A to E, with D and E the lowest.
explanation.definitionFit: A detractor disparages others, a synonym of critic.
